note: The age a seat on a town, city, village or county governing body (council, commission, board of trustees or aldermen) asks of a candidate where the place's own rule has not been read. State municipal and county codes most commonly open these seats to any qualified elector of the place, and a qualified elector is eighteen. One row serves all 56 places until a place's own rule is read into its candidacy pack.
estimatedFrom: State codes opening a local governing-body seat to a qualified elector of the place (A.R.S. 9-232; KRS 83A.040; Tex. Elec. Code 141.001; RCW 36.32.010), with the voting age of eighteen under U.S. Const. amend. XXVI

examples.citation: A.R.S. 9-232: a council member must be eighteen at the election and a qualified elector residing in the city or town
KRS 83A.040, as city codes carry it: a council member shall be at least 18 years of age and a qualified voter in the city
Tex. Elec. Code 141.001: a candidate for public elective office must be 18 or older and a registered voter
RCW 36.32.010: each board of county commissioners shall consist of three qualified electors
